Name: Pashur, Son of Immer
Role: Priest; Chief Governor of the Temple
Summary: Pashur, son of Immer the priest, was chief governor in the house of the Lord. When Jeremiah prophesied in the temple court, Pashur struck him and put him in the stocks overnight. Jeremiah renamed him Magor-missabib — terror on every side — and foretold his captivity in Babylon.
KeyStory: Pashur smote Jeremiah and put him in the stocks at the high gate of Benjamin, and in the morning Jeremiah told him his name would be Terror on every side.
LifeLesson: Using temple authority to punish a prophet turns the punisher into the prophecy's example.
